intent: Stop the Python tests workflow installing ~62 linters and formatters it never invokes, by giving it a requirements file scoped to what the suite actually needs.
scope: Non-goal: changing pre-commit.yml, which genuinely needs every formatter
changes: Added meta/requirements-test.txt: 17 packages, down from 79. Derived by static import analysis over python_pkg/ and linux_configuration/tests/, then verified by running the suite against only that list.
python-tests.yml installs the subset, caches on it, and lists it in both path filters so a change to it triggers the workflow.
Added a requirements-test-sync pre-commit hook reusing check_requirements_sync.py's existing --requirements flag, so a new third-party import cannot silently break CI with a ModuleNotFoundError.
The pytest-* plugins are included deliberately: randomly, timeout, sugar and xdist change how the suite runs even though nothing imports them.

verification.command: python3.11 venv + pip install -r meta/requirements-test.txt + full pytest run with coverage
verification.evidence: 2174 passed, TOTAL 100.00%, 7138 statements / 1748 branches, 0 missing -- identical to the full-requirements run
6.2s for 17 packages against a warm local cache; the full 79-package list took 49-55s on the CI runner
exit 0 -- every third-party import in python_pkg is declared in the subset

risks: A new runtime import that is not added here would fail CI. Mitigated by the new hook, which gates on the same analysis and runs on every python_pkg .py change.
The subset can drift from the full list's version bounds. Both are >= ranges on the same packages, so a divergence surfaces as a resolver conflict rather than a silent mismatch.
rollback: Point the Install dependencies step and cache-dependency-path back at requirements.txt and delete the hook.
After rollback, confirm the install step returns to ~50s.
